extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners preparing appeals and appeal briefs before the USPTO (Board/PTAB) and USPTO examiners/staff administering appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for requesting pre-appeal brief conferences and for preparing and filing appeal briefs and related procedures before the USPTO (37 CFR 41.37 and related MPEP sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Conference Request: scope and content limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests are limited to appealable, not petitionable matters. An after final amendment may not accompany the request. Any amendment pursuant to 37 CFR 1.116 filed on the same day as the Pre-Appeal Brief Conference Request, regardless of whether the amendment is filed together with the notice of appeal and request or in a separate submission, will be considered to accompany the request and therefore will not meet the content requirements of the Pilot program. A request that fails to comply with these requirements should be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pre-appeal brief request found not compliant cannot be corrected and resubmitted because a corrected request would not meet the requirement that the notice of appeal and pre-appeal brief request be filed on the same date. If applicant files notice of appeal, Pre-Appeal Brief Conference Request, and an RCE on the same date, the RCE controls; a notice of appeal cannot be entered into an application with an RCE until the application is under rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Conference: panel composition and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of a properly filed request, a supervisor will designate a panel of appropriate reviewers to review the appellant's remarks and the examiner's rejections. The panel will include at least a supervisor and the examiner of record and will have the authority to reopen prosecution if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appellant will not be permitted to attend the review and no interviews will be granted prior to issuance of the pre-appeal brief review decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Conference: possible panel decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: After the review is complete, the Office will mail a decision stating one of the following: (A) The application remains under appeal because there is at least one actual issue for appeal. (B) Prosecution on the merits is reopened and an appropriate Office communication will follow. (C) The application is allowed on the existing claims and prosecution remains closed. (D) The request fails to comply with the submission requirements and is dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In appropriate circumstances, a proposed amendment may accompany the panel’s decision proposing changes that, if accepted, may result in an indication of allowability for the contested claim(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Brief Conference: events terminating the panel review
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel’s review will be terminated if the applicant files any of the following responses after filing a request but prior to a decision by the panel: (A) An appeal brief. (B) A request for continued examination. (C) An after final amendment. (D) An affidavit or other evidence. (E) An express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing any of these items after the request but before the panel decision ends the pre-appeal review; subsequent actions follow the normal appeal/prosecution processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of pre-appeal decision on appeal brief timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After a panel decision, the time period for filing an appeal brief will be reset to be one month from the mailing of the decision on the request, or the balance of the two-month time period running from the receipt of the notice of appeal, whichever is greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further, the time period for filing of the appeal brief is extendible under 37 CFR 1.136. For as long as the pilot program remains in effect, submission of a pre-appeal review request may extend the period for filing an appeal brief until a decision is made on the request or the request is otherwise dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after notice of appeal: general rule and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: One interview after final rejection is normally permitted (the time from mailing of final rejection through filing of an appeal brief). However, no interviews will be granted from the filing of a request for pre-appeal review through issuance of a decision on the request. Except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the appeal brief is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews after an examiner’s answer and prior to payment of the appeal forwarding fee are likely to confuse the record and are not permitted except in unusual circumstances (e.g., appellant wishes to cancel all appealed claims and proceed to issue with claims previously indicated as allowable, or where the examiner is convinced some claims are in condition for allowance). Requests for interviews on cases under Board jurisdiction require specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a written showing of extraordinary circumstances to justify remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the Official Record on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The official record on appeal contains the items listed in the content listing of the Image File Wrapper or the official file of the Office if other than the Image File Wrapper, excluding amendments, Evidence, and other documents that were not entered or indicated considered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases where physical items are not scanned into the Image File Wrapper (e.g., original drawings, sequence listings), the Image File Wrapper will include an entry pointing to the artifact file. An IDS or form PTO-892 indicated as having been considered by the examiner is included in the Record even if the individual references do not appear separately in the content listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dictionaries and 'Evidence' on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of appeal, 'Evidence' does not encompass dictionaries, which may be cited before the Board. Evidence is defined to exclude dictionaries so appellants and examiners may refer to dictionaries in briefs and examiner answers without treating those references as evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding dictionaries from 'Evidence' allows the Board and tribunals to consult dictionaries as aids to understanding; case law (e.g., Phillips v. AWH) supports consultation of dictionaries when construing claim terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief filing deadline (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file a brief under 37 CFR 41.37 within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal under § 41.31. The Office date of receipt of the notice of appeal (not the Certificate of Mailing date) is the date from which this two-month period is measured. If the notice of appeal is filed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10 using USPS Priority Mail Express, the date of deposit is the receipt date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.37(a) does not permit the brief to be filed within the time allowed for reply to the action from which the appeal was taken. The two-month period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 (or 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination); extensions beyond 5 months generally require extraordinary circumstances under 1.136(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to timely file an appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: On failure to file the brief within the period specified, the appeal will stand dismissed. If there are allowed claims, those claims are not lost by dismissal; if no claims are allowed, the application is abandoned as of the date the brief was due. In ex parte reexamination, failure to file the brief results in issuance of the certificate under 37 CFR 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is abandoned after dismissal, appellant may petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 and must file either an RCE (with appropriate submission and fee) or an appeal brief with any required fees to reinstate the appeal; a proper brief must be filed before the petition will be considered on its merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief required contents (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) headings and order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided, the brief shall contain the following items under appropriate headings in the order indicated: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals, interferences, and trials; (iii) Summary of claimed subject matter; (iv) Argument; (v) Claims appendix. A brief filed by an appellant not represented by a registered practitioner need only substantially comply with (i), (ii), (iv), and (v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief must set forth arguments and the basis therefor, with citations of statutes, regulations, authorities and parts of the Record relied upon. The brief must have required items under appropriate headings in the specified order; however, headings are not required when items are not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by name the real party in interest at the time the appeal brief is filed, except that such statement is not required if the named inventor(s) are the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omitted, the Office may assume the named inventor(s) are the real party in interest. Identification allows Board members to comply with ethics/conflict-of-interest rules. Example wording provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of related appeals, interferences, and trials
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by application, patent, appeal, interference, or trial number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences, trials before the Board, or judicial proceedings which (1) involve an application or patent owned by the appellant or assignee, (2) are known to appellant or representative, and (3) may be related to or have a bearing on the Board’s decision in the pending appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are no such related cases, the statement is not required and, if omitted, the Office may assume there are no related cases. The rule does not require copies of decisions in related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each of the rejected independent claims, referring to the specification in the Record by page and line number or paragraph number, and to the drawings by reference characters. For claims with means-plus-function (35 U.S.C. 112(f)), the concise explanation must identify the structure, material, or acts described in the specification corresponding to each claimed function with specific record references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to the patent application publication does not satisfy this paragraph. Each rejected independent claim must be summarized; dependent claims argued separately must also have the corresponding identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument content and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The arguments of appellant with respect to each ground of rejection, and the basis therefor, with citations of the statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the Record relied on. The arguments shall explain why the examiner erred as to each ground of rejection contested by appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each ground of rejection contested must be argued under a separate heading reasonably identifying the ground (e.g., claim number, statutory basis, applied reference). For grounds applying to multiple claims, appellant may argue separately, as a group, or as a subgroup; failure to separately argue grouped claims is a waiver of separate patentability arguments. A statement merely pointing out what a claim recites is insufficient. Except as provided in §§ 41.41, 41.47 and 41.52, any arguments or authorities not included in the appeal brief will be refused consideration by the Board for the present appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal must be included with the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required; the brief and every other document relating to an appeal should indicate the Technology Center number and application/reexamination control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new or non-admitted amendments or evidence in the brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other Evidence. See 37 CFR 1.116 for treatment of amendments, affidavits or other evidence filed after final action but before or on the same date of filing an appeal and § 41.33 for treatment of amendments, affidavits or other Evidence filed after the date of filing the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of an examiner's refusal to admit an amendment or Evidence is by petition to the Director (37 CFR 1.181). An amendment or other evidence submitted under 37 CFR 1.116 or 37 CFR 41.33 will not be entered as part of the record for the appeal unless entered by the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of non-compliance and opportunity to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with all requirements of 37 CFR 41.37(c), appellant will be notified of the reasons for non-compliance and given a time period within which to file an amended brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant does not file an amended brief that overcomes all stated reasons within the set time period, the appeal will stand dismissed. Review of a determination of non-compliance is by petition to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge (37 CFR 41.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for filing the appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods set forth for filing the appeal brief are extendable under the provisions of 37 CFR 1.136 for patent applications and 37 CFR 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition for extension under 1.136(a) with fee may be filed; additional time in excess of 5 months will not be granted unless extraordinary circumstances under 1.136(b) are shown. When a petition for extension is granted, the new due date is computed from the receipt date of the notice of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro se appellant exception to certain content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief filed by an appellant who is not represented by a registered practitioner need only substantially comply with paragraphs (c)(1)(i) (real party in interest), (c)(1)(ii) (related cases), (c)(1)(iv) (argument), and (c)(1)(v) (claims appendix) of 37 CFR 41.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The headings are not required when items are not applicable. The pro se brief which does not contain all items will be accepted so long as it substantially complies with the specified subparagraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix strongly encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: While no longer a requirement to include an evidence appendix, the Office strongly encourages and appreciates receiving copies of the evidence relied upon (e.g., copies of declarations and affidavits, evidence of secondary considerations, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing copies ensures the Board considers the proper evidence and avoids confusion as to which evidence is referenced. Alternatively, appellants should clearly identify the evidence relied upon with a description and the date of entry into the Image File Wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to address every ground of rejection (waiver rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s brief must present arguments responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner in the Office action from which the appeal has been taken (as modified by any advisory action and/or pre-appeal brief conference decision). If a ground of rejection is not addressed in the brief, appellant has waived any challenge to that ground and the Board may summarily sustain it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant cannot rely on asserting a ground is 'clearly improper' without explaining why the examiner erred; requesting that a rejection be held in abeyance (e.g., non-statutory double patenting) does not meet 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv) and will be treated as a waiver. The Board may decide appeals as to grouped claims on a single selected claim if appellant groups claims together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained brief requirement (no incorporation by reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief should not incorporate or reference previous responses; 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) requires that the brief set forth arguments and the basis therefor so that no search of the Record is required to determine appellant's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral argument will not remedy deficiencies in a brief. The Board posts checklists to assist in reducing non-compliant briefs. Failure to include required material may result in notice of non-compliance and possible dismissal.
